title: High Molecular Weight DNA Extraction from Bacteria using NEB Monarch Kit
author: Ben Pascoe
materials: NEB Monarch HMW DNA extraction kit
Review the complete protocol before beginning.

· Microcentrifuge · Thermal mixer containing a 1.5 ml tube block (optional: 2 ml tube block for elution) · Recommended: vertical rotating mixer (e.g., Thermo Scientific‱ HulaMixer‱ Sample Mixer). · Ethanol (≥ 95%). · Cold PBS, 300 µl per sample (Low Input: 150 µl per sample). Alternatively, TE or Tris buffer can be used. · Isopropanol, 550 µl per sample (Low Input: 275 µl/sample). · 1.5 ml DNase-free, low DNA binding microfuge tubes (e.g., Eppendorf‱ DNA LoBind‱, #0030108051) are recommended for elution and storage (1 per sample); it is especially important to use low DNA binding tubes if working with UHMW DNA, which tends to bind to plastic surfaces. · For Gram-negative bacteria: Lysozyme (25 mg/ml, 10 µl per sample) · For Gram-positive bacteria: STET Buffer (Current Protocols in Molecular Biology) containing Lysozyme (10 mg/ml) can be an effective lysis agent (150 µl or 300 µl per sample). · Additional lysis agents may be required (e.g., lysostaphin).

steps.title: Prepare bench and safety
steps.instruction: Clean all active workbenches with 80 % ethanol, wear appropriate personal protective clothing, organise the bench by removing clutter, avoid exposing sterile materials to airborne contaminants, and treat all isolates as infectious following local GLP and safety guidelines.

steps.title: Pre‑heat thermal mixer blocks
steps.instruction: Set the thermal mixer with a 1.5 ml block to 37 °C. If a second block is available, pre‑heat it to 56 °C for later steps.

steps.title: Add ethanol to wash buffer
steps.instruction: Add ethanol (≥ 95 %) to the gDNA Wash Buffer according to the volume indicated on the bottle label.

steps.title: Pellet bacterial cells
steps.instruction: Transfer the bacterial culture into a Monarch Pestle Tube and centrifuge at maximum speed (12 000 × g, 1 min, temperature not specified). If a rotor‑stator homogenizer will be used, place the pellet in a compatible 2 ml tube (not supplied).

steps.title: Lyse Gram‑negative bacteria
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 300 µL cold PBS (use 150 µL for Low Input) or cold TE/Tris, add 10 µL Lysozyme (25 mg mL⁻¹, not supplied) and vortex briefly, add 300 µL HMW gDNA Tissue Lysis Buffer (150 µL for Low Input) and invert 5–10 times, then incubate at 37 °C in the thermal mixer:

substeps.instruction: Maximum agitation speed (≈ 2000 rpm) for standard fragment size (50–250 kb).
Low agitation speed (≈ 500 rpm) for maximal DNA size; incubation time ≈ 5 min for E. coli at 2000 rpm, longer at 500 rpm.

steps.title: Lyse Gram‑positive bacteria
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 300 µL appropriate lysis buffer containing a lytic enzyme (150 µL for Low Input) and vortex briefly; STET buffer with freshly added lysozyme (10 mg mL⁻¹) works for some Bacillus spp., incubate at 37 °C for 30 min without agitation, then add 300 µL HMW gDNA Tissue Lysis Buffer (150 µL for Low Input) and invert 5–10 times.

steps.title: Increase temperature to 56 °C
steps.instruction: If only one thermal mixer is available, after the 37 °C lysozyme step raise the block temperature to 56 °C.

steps.title: Add Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL Proteinase K (10 µL for Low Input) to the lysate and invert 10–20 times to mix.

steps.title: Homogenize (thermal mixer)
steps.instruction: Incubate the sample at 56 °C for 30 min in the thermal mixer at the desired speed:

substeps.instruction: For standard ONT ligation protocols use maximum speed (≈ 2000 rpm) to obtain 50–250 kb fragments.
For maximal DNA size use a low speed (< 500 rpm); speeds < 500 rpm are not recommended.

steps.title: Homogenize (rotor‑stator)
steps.instruction: Place the lysate in a 2 ml tube, insert the rotor‑stator probe on the lowest setting, and homogenize for 5–15 s, stopping when foam appears. Extend homogenization if needed to reach the desired 50–250 kb size.

steps.title: Incubate after transfer
steps.instruction: Transfer the lysate to a 1.5 ml Pestle Tube and incubate at 56 °C for at least 30 min in the thermal mixer at maximum speed (≈ 2000 rpm).

steps.title: Add RNase A
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL RNase A (5 µL for Low Input) and invert 5–10 times, then incubate for 10 min at 56 °C with agitation at the same speed used in the previous step.

steps.title: Swap heat block for 2 ml tube
steps.instruction: Replace the thermal‑mixer block with one that accommodates a 2 ml tube and pre‑heat to 56 °C. If a 2 ml block is unavailable, continue using the 1.5 ml block.

steps.title: Add Protein Separation Solution
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL Protein Separation Solution (150 µL for Low Input) to the tube, mix by inverting for 1 min, or use a vertical rotating mixer at 20 rpm.

steps.title: Phase‑separation centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 10 min at 16 000 × g. The mixture will separate into a clear upper DNA phase and a lower protein phase (possible white precipitate). If separation is incomplete, centrifuge an additional 20 min.

steps.title: Prepare plastics for multiple samples
steps.instruction: For each sample, label and arrange: a Monarch Collection Tube II, a Monarch Bead Retainer (inserted), two Monarch 2 ml tubes (one for phase separation, one for elution), and a 1.5 ml low‑bind microfuge tube (DNA low‑bind, not supplied).

steps.title: Transfer aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Using a 1000 µL wide‑bore tip (200 µL tip for the final volume), transfer the clear upper phase (≈ 800 µL; ≈ 400 µL for Low Input) to a labeled Monarch 2 ml tube, avoiding the protein layer. If the total volume is < 700 µL (< 350 µL for Low Input), note that the isopropanol volume in the binding step must be adjusted to 0.7 × the sample volume.

steps.title: Add DNA Capture Beads
steps.instruction: Using clean forceps, add 2 DNA Capture Beads to each Monarch 2 ml tube containing the transferred aqueous phase.

steps.title: Bind DNA to beads
steps.instruction: Add 550 µL isopropanol (275 µL for Low Input), close the cap, and mix:

substeps.instruction: If a vertical rotating mixer is available, rotate at 10 rpm for 5 min.
Otherwise, invert the tube slowly and gently 25–30 times (each inversion ≈ 5–6 s). Continue inverting until the solution is no longer viscous and DNA is visibly wrapped around the beads.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Discard the liquid without disturbing the bead‑DNA complex. Choose one of two methods:

substeps.instruction: Keep the tube upright, insert a pipette tip, gently push the beads aside and aspirate the liquid.
Angle the tube so beads settle at the bottom, aspirate from the liquid surface while the tube is nearly horizontal.

steps.title: First wash of beads
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL gDNA Wash Buffer, close the cap, and invert the tube 2–3 times. Remove the wash buffer as described in the previous step.

steps.title: Second wash of beads
steps.instruction: Repeat the 500 µL gDNA Wash Buffer wash and remove the buffer by pipetting or decanting (complete removal is not required).

steps.title: Transfer beads to bead retainer
steps.instruction: Place a labeled bead retainer into a Monarch Collection Tube II, pour the beads from the 2 ml tube into the retainer, close the cap, and discard the used 2 ml tube. Close the cap after each transfer when handling multiple samples.

steps.title: Pulse‑spin to remove residual buffer
steps.instruction: Spin the collection tube in a benchtop minicentrifuge for ≤ 1 s to expel any remaining wash buffer from the beads.

steps.title: Prepare beads for elution
steps.instruction: Separate the bead retainer from the collection tube, pour the beads into a new labeled Monarch 2 ml tube, and insert the used bead retainer into a labeled 1.5 ml low‑bind microfuge tube (DNA low‑bind) for later elution. Discard the empty collection tube.

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL Elution Buffer II (10 mM Tris, pH 9.0, 0.5 mM EDTA) onto the beads, close the cap, and incubate for a minimum of 5 min at 56 °C in the thermal mixer at the lowest speed (≈ 300 rpm). Halfway through, tilt the tube almost horizontally and gently shake to keep beads suspended. Elution volume may be reduced to 50 µL; if using < 100 µL, shake the tube several times during incubation.

steps.title: Collect eluate
steps.instruction: Insert the bead retainer (containing the beads) into the 1.5 ml microfuge tube, pour the eluate and beads into the retainer, close the cap, and spin briefly if any liquid remains in the 2 ml tube.

steps.title: Separate eluate from beads
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 30 s at 12 000 × g to pellet the beads; discard the beads and the bead retainer.

steps.title: Finalize DNA solution
steps.instruction: After incubation, pipette the eluate again 5–10 times. Store short‑term at 4 °C (weeks) or long‑term at –20 °C. The elution buffer (10 mM Tris, pH 9.0, 0.5 mM EDTA) supports long‑term storage.
